rows.stem: Which of the following is *not* a thermal decomposition reaction ?
rows.solution:
A thermal decomposition reaction is one in which a single substance breaks down into simpler substances on heating. Ferrous sulphate, calcium carbonate (limestone) and lead nitrate all decompose when heated, so those three reactions are thermal decompositions.

Silver chloride decomposes when it is exposed to sunlight, not on heating. It is a photolytic decomposition (the reaction used in black and white photography):

\(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

The lead nitrate equation is printed without the 2 in front of \(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2}\), so as printed it is unbalanced. The balanced equation is

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO + 4NO_2 + O_2}\)

This does not change the answer: it is still a thermal decomposition.

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{2\,AgCl \longrightarrow 2\,Ag + Cl_2}\).

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem: Identify an involuntary action from the following :
rows.solution:
An involuntary action takes place without our thinking about it or willing it. The heart goes on beating regularly whether we think about it or not; this is controlled by the medulla in the hind-brain. Riding a bicycle, picking up a pencil and walking in a straight line are all voluntary actions, which we decide to do.

This is option (C) Regular beating of heart.

rows.stem:
Identify the functional group present in the following compounds and also name them :

(a) Structure (a) as printed; see the attached figure.

(b) Structure (b) as printed; see the attached figure.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - both compounds are given only as drawn structural formulas, (a) a two-carbon structure and (b) a one-carbon structure, with every atom and bond shown; the groups bonded to each carbon are what the question asks the student to identify and name, so they are not typed here (structures are figures, and describing them would state the answer). Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
(a) The compound is \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\): a carbon carrying three hydrogens joined to a carbon that is double-bonded to oxygen and also carries an OH group. The functional group is the carboxylic acid group, \(\mathrm{{-}COOH}\), and the compound is ethanoic acid.

(b) The compound is \(\mathrm{HCHO}\): one carbon double-bonded to oxygen and joined to two hydrogens. The functional group is the aldehyde group, \(\mathrm{{-}CHO}\), and the compound is methanal (formaldehyde).

rows.stem: Explain how the original number of chromosomes present in the parents are restored in the progeny. Name the cell division by which chromosome number is maintained in the progeny.
rows.solution:
Parents produce germ cells (gametes) in specialised reproductive organs. Through meiosis these germ cells get only half the number of chromosomes found in the non-reproductive body cells.

During sexual reproduction a male germ cell fuses with a female germ cell to form the zygote. Each brings half the set, so the zygote, and the progeny that grows from it, gets back the original number of chromosomes of the parents.

The cell division is meiosis (reduction division): it halves the chromosome number in the germ cells, which is what keeps the number the same from one generation to the next.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: Define power of a lens. Find power of a lens whose focal length is 50 cm.
rows.solution:
The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length expressed in metres. It is the degree of convergence or divergence of light rays achieved by the lens. Its SI unit is the dioptre (D).

Focal length \(f = 50\) cm \(= 0{\cdot}5\) m, so

\(P = \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{0{\cdot}5} = \dfrac{100}{50} = 2\) D.

The power is \(+2\) D for a converging (convex) lens; a diverging lens of the same focal length would have a power of \(-2\) D.

rows.stem: An electric source can supply a charge of 750 coulomb. If the current drawn by a device is 15 mA, find the time in which the electric source will be discharged completely.
rows.solution:
Charge \(Q = 750\) C and current \(I = 15\) mA \(= 15 \times 10^{-3}\) A. Since \(Q = I \times t\),

\(t = \dfrac{Q}{I} = \dfrac{750}{15 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{750 \times 1000}{15} = 50000\) s.

The source is discharged completely in 50000 s (about 13.9 hours).

rows.stem: Suggest an activity to differentiate between the chemical properties (acidic or basic character) of the product obtained on burning a metal (magnesium) and a non-metal (sulphur).
rows.solution:
Activity:

1. Hold a magnesium ribbon with tongs and burn it in a flame. Collect the white ash (magnesium oxide) and dissolve it in a little water.

\(\mathrm{2Mg + O_2 \rightarrow 2MgO}\)

\(\mathrm{MgO + H_2O \rightarrow Mg(OH)_2}\)

2. Take some sulphur powder in a deflagrating spoon and burn it. Collect the fumes (sulphur dioxide) in a test tube or gas jar and add a little water to it.

\(\mathrm{S + O_2 \rightarrow SO_2}\)

\(\mathrm{SO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow H_2SO_3}\)

3. Test each solution with blue and red litmus solution (or paper).

Observations: the magnesium solution turns red litmus blue, and blue litmus remains blue. The sulphur solution turns blue litmus red, and red litmus remains red.

Inference: the oxide of the metal (magnesium oxide) is basic in nature, while the oxide of the non-metal (sulphur dioxide) is acidic in nature.

rows.stem:
A plant with violet flowers (VV) was crossed with a plant with white flowers (vv).

(a) What colour of flowers was obtained in the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation and why ?

(b) Write the percentage of plants with white flowers in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation plants, if \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants were self-pollinated. Give reason why this trait was not expressed in \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation.

(c) In what ratio did we get the plants with (VV) and (Vv) gene combination in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation ?
rows.solution:
(a) The \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants all had violet flowers. Each \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plant is Vv, and the gene for violet colour (V) is dominant over the gene for white colour (v), so violet is expressed.

(b) Self-pollinating the Vv plants gives VV : Vv : vv in the ratio \(1 : 2 : 1\). Only vv plants have white flowers, so 25% of the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) plants have white flowers.

White colour was not expressed in \(\mathrm{F_1}\) because the gene for white colour is recessive: it cannot express itself in the presence of the dominant gene for violet colour.

(c) In \(\mathrm{F_2}\), VV : Vv \(= 1 : 2\).

rows.stem: “Earth wire is a safety measure in domestic electric circuits.” Justify this statement explaining its role in case of accidental leakage of electric appliances.
rows.solution:
Earthing is a safety measure especially for appliances with a metallic body, such as an electric iron, toaster or refrigerator. The metallic body of such an appliance is connected to the earth wire, which is joined to a metal plate buried deep in the earth near the house.

The earth wire provides a low-resistance conducting path for the current. If, by accident, the live wire touches the metallic body (a leakage of current), the current flows straight to the earth through this path, and the body is kept at the potential of the earth.

So a person who touches the appliance does not get a severe electric shock. (The large current through the earth wire also usually blows the fuse, cutting off the supply.)

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: Explain chlor-alkali process and write balanced chemical equations for the reactions that occur. Name the gases obtained at the anode and cathode respectively. Mention two uses each of the two gases obtained in the above process.
rows.solution:
When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine), it decomposes to form sodium hydroxide, chlorine and hydrogen. The process is called the chlor-alkali process because its products are chlorine (chlor) and sodium hydroxide (alkali).

\(\mathrm{2NaCl(aq) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq) + Cl_2(g) + H_2(g)}\)

Chlorine gas is given off at the anode and hydrogen gas at the cathode. Sodium hydroxide solution is formed near the cathode.

Uses of chlorine (any two): for making bleaching powder; for making drinking water free from germs (water treatment and swimming pools); for making PVC, pesticides and CFCs.

Uses of hydrogen (any two): for making ammonia for fertilisers; as a fuel; for making margarine (hydrogenation of oils).

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: Common salt is a very important raw material as many compounds of industrial use can be prepared from it. Explain, giving chemical equations, the method of preparation of washing soda from sodium chloride. List four industrial/domestic uses of washing soda.
rows.solution:
1. A concentrated solution of sodium chloride (brine) reacts with ammonia and carbon dioxide, giving sodium hydrogen carbonate and ammonium chloride:

\(\mathrm{NaCl + NH_3 + CO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow NaHCO_3 + NH_4Cl}\)

2. When sodium hydrogen carbonate is heated strongly, sodium carbonate is obtained:

\(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Na_2CO_3 + CO_2 + H_2O}\)

3. Sodium carbonate is recrystallised from water to give washing soda, which carries ten molecules of water of crystallisation:

\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 + 10H_2O \rightarrow Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\)

Uses of washing soda:

1. In the glass, soap and paper industries.

2. In the manufacture of sodium compounds such as borax.

3. As a cleaning agent for domestic purposes.

4. For removing permanent hardness of water.
